title: The $6,000 credit card mistake that takes 21 years

beats.say: Your six thousand dollar credit card balance takes two hundred fifty-two months to clear.
beats.visual: A sleek dark credit card resting on a clean wooden table under a single warm spotlight, macro shot.

beats.say: That is twenty-one years of minimum payments at twenty-four percent annual percentage rate.
beats.visual: An old brass desk calendar slowly flipping pages in dim lighting, shallow depth of field.

beats.say: Stay until the end to see the exact cost of this quiet trap.
beats.visual: A pair of hands sliding a leather wallet into the dark pocket of a wool coat.

beats.say: Most people look at the minimum due and assume the bank is just helping them out.
beats.visual: A close-up of a pen signing a paper statement on a dark mahogany desk.

beats.say: That minimum is calculated as one percent of the balance plus the monthly interest.
beats.visual: A vintage mechanical calculator sitting on a textured concrete surface, side view.

beats.say: But here is the part nobody mentions about how debt actually compounds.
beats.visual: A hand sliding a silver chess piece across a dark polished board, cinematic side light.

beats.say: At twenty-four percent interest, debt doubles every three years.
beats.visual: A dark analog clock ticking in a quiet room, blurred background, moody ambiance.

beats.say: By the time you finish paying off that six thousand dollars, you hand over ten thousand eight hundred eighty-seven dollars in interest alone.
beats.visual: Counting a stack of crisp hundred-dollar bills under low amber light, overhead view.

beats.say: That is nearly double the original purchase just for borrowing time.
beats.visual: A shadow cast against a bare concrete wall by a single hanging bulb.

beats.say: Now compare that to paying three hundred dollars a month instead.
beats.visual: A banking app open on a dark smartphone screen resting on a dark slate counter.

beats.say: The timeline drops from twenty-one years down to just twenty-six months.
beats.visual: A hand closing a heavy laptop lid in a dimly lit minimalist workspace.

beats.say: Total interest plummets to one thousand seven hundred thirty-nine dollars.
beats.visual: A modern coffee mug sitting next to a closed notebook on a dark wood table.

beats.say: The bank relies on your patience expiring, and that is exactly how
beats.visual: A person walking away down a long dimly lit hallway, shot from behind.

caption:
The math behind credit card minimum payments is designed to keep you paying for decades. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.

#money #personalfinance #debtfree #financialliteracy #creditcards
description: Discover the hidden math behind paying only the minimum on a $6,000 credit card balance at 24% APR and how changing your monthly payment alters the timeline.
first_comment: What surprised you the most about this calculation?

facts.claim: $6,000 credit card at 24% APR paying only the minimum takes 252 months (~21 years) and costs $10,887 in interest.
facts.basis: Money fact sheet calculated at 1% + interest, min $25.

facts.claim: Same $6,000 at 24% paying $300/month takes 26 months and $1,739 interest.
At 24% debt doubles every 3 years according to the Rule of 72.
